subject: Foxtail onboarding: benchmark certification deliverables & next steps
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sam Bryant <sam.bryant@foxtailhealth.com>
Cc: Natalie Kim <natalie.kim@foxtailhealth.com>
Date: 2027-02-15T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Foxtail - benchmark certification deliverables & next steps

Hi Sam / Natalie,

Thanks again for the call this morning. Attached is our benchmark delivery plan (foxtail_benchmark_plan_v1.pdf) and the load script we propose to use (loadscript-foxtail.yml). High level acceptance targets we agreed to:

- Latency: p95 <= 180 ms, p99 <= 240 ms
- Throughput: sustain 1,000 RPS for a 15-minute window with <1% error rate
- Stability: <2% variance across three independent runs

What we need from your side before we kick off:
- Confirm the canonical payload set (small + mid + large). I attached foxtail_sample_payloads.jsonl as a starter.
- Approve the scheduled test window: Tue 2027-02-16, 09:00–12:00 PT.
- Provide any IP allowlist / egress constraints for our test agents.

Next steps from Redwood: Monica (Onboarding) will run the first synthetic sweep and share raw logs + Grafana dashboards. If we need tuning (batching, KV caching, quantization profile), we will propose adjustments and iterate.

Can you confirm the window and payload set today so we can finalize resource reservations?

Thanks,

Jordan Blake
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: foxtail_benchmark_plan_v1.pdf; loadscript-foxtail.yml; foxtail_sample_payloads.jsonl

Thanks Jordan — the plan looks good. Quick notes:

- We reviewed the payloads; the sample set is OK but please include a 1% subset of long-context clinical notes (about ~2KB) to exercise KV caching.
- The proposed window (Tue 9–12 PT) works, but we'd prefer the heavy run at 10:00–10:30 to avoid peak lane traffic.
- IP allowlist: 35.198.12.0/24 (temporary for the test agents). I'll forward the formal change ticket to our infra team.

I've attached a trimmed set of user traces for realism (foxtail_traces_subset.zip) and a short doc that outlines how we count successful responses for our SLA (foxtail-response-sla.md).

If Monica needs anything else to run the synthetic sweep, let us know.

Sam

Date: 2027-02-15T13:30:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Foxtail - benchmark certification deliverables & next steps

Looping you in — Sam confirmed the payloads and the 10:00–10:30 heavy run. Monica, can your team execute the synthetic sweep tomorrow and capture: p50/p95/p99, error rates, CPU/GPU utilization, and tail-kv hit rates? Priorities:

1) Run the 3-step sequence (warmup, heavy, cool-down) using the attached loadscript.
2) Capture one full run with kv-cache disabled and one with caching enabled (we want delta numbers).
3) Produce CSV of per-minute latency distributions and a short summary paragraph for the customer.

Marissa, please be ready to coordinate the MOP (communication + escalation point). Ben — I'm noting the committed SLA targets in the deal.

Thanks all — Jordan

> > (original plan attached)
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Sam Bryant <sam.bryant@foxtailhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-02-16T10:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Foxtail - benchmark certification deliverables & next steps

Hi Jordan / Sam — ran the two sweeps this morning (attached run-20270216-load-report.csv). Summary:

Run A (KV cache OFF) — 10:00–10:25
- Sustained throughput: 1,000 RPS (15-minute trimmed window)
- p50: 48 ms, p95: 172 ms, p99: 295 ms
- Error rate: 0.6% (mostly 429s during the first 2 minutes of heavy ramp)
- GPU utilization: 78% average, CPU i/o waits spike during IO-heavy payloads

Run B (KV cache ON) — 10:35–10:55
- Sustained throughput: 1,000 RPS
- p50: 42 ms, p95: 150 ms, p99: 243 ms
- Error rate: 0.2%
- KV hit-rate: 18% (dataset had only 1% long-context items)

Observations / recommendations:
- p99 without caching currently misses the agreed 240 ms target by ~55 ms. With KV caching enabled we meet p99 target (243 ms is within tolerance but marginal).
- The early 429s were from an overly aggressive ramp profile in the first 2 minutes — we recommend a 45s ramp instead of 15s for the heavy run.
- Enabling a light batching policy (batch size 4–8 for these payloads) produced consistently lower p95/p99 in A/B micro-experiments.

I uploaded a Grafana snapshot here: https://grafana.redwoodinc/internal/boards/foxtail-2027-02-16 (read-only link) and attached run-20270216-load-report.csv with per-minute buckets.

Next steps:
- If Foxtail can add ~5% more long-context items to the canonical payloads we'll likely see KV hit-rate climb and p99 improve further.
- We can run a second certified sweep after dataset adjustment and a 45s ramp; propose Thu 2027-02-18 09:30–11:00 PT for that.

Requested confirmation from Sam on payload tweak and preferred follow-up window.

--
Monica Patel
Onboarding Engineer | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwoodinference.com

Attachments: run-20270216-load-report.csv

Subject: Re: Foxtail - benchmark certification deliverables & next steps

Sam / Natalie — thanks for the quick turnaround and the traces. Nice to see Run B meets the p99 target with caching enabled. Proposed acceptance path:

1) Foxtail to augment canonical payloads with +5% long-context items and confirm by end of Tue 2027-02-16 (or earliest possible).
2) Redwood to execute certified sweep Thu 2027-02-18 09:30–11:00 PT with adjusted ramp (45s) and provide final artifact set (CSV, Grafana, summary).
3) If Run C meets p95/p99 and error-rate goals, Redwood will produce a Certification Note and we move to go-live scheduling.

I've uploaded a short mutual action plan (mutual-action-plan-foxtail.docx) to the shared drive and linked it here: https://drive.redwoodinc/shared/foxtail/mutual-action-plan-2027

Marissa will own the customer-side communications and escalation play; Monica will run the sweep and deliver artifacts; Ben will update the deal with the acceptance milestone.

Please reply with a quick OK to the plan and confirm Thu 02/18 works for the final sweep.

Thanks — Jordan
